metadata.case_name: Ganesh Haribhau Hol vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another
metadata.court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Circuit Bench at Kolhapur

facts.text: The applicant, Ganesh Haribhau Hol, filed an anticipatory bail application in connection with Crime No. 216/2025 registered with Koregaon Police Station, District Satara, for offences under Sections 69 and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

The prosecution alleges that after the informant's husband's death in 2013, she organized a Satyanarayan Pooja and invited doctors, including the accused, where the accused became acquainted with the informant.
The accused disclosed to the informant in 2013 that he loved her and wanted to marry her, but she refused due to her responsibility to raise two children.
The accused repeatedly met the informant, claimed matrimonial disputes with his wife and intention to divorce, leading the informant to decide to marry him.
After the informant agreed, the accused demanded physical relations; initially she refused, but later consented under the pretext of marriage and divorce, leading to repeated sexual relations.
Between 17 January 2019 and September 2024, the accused repeatedly committed sexual assault on the victim under the pretext of marriage and assurance of divorce.
The FIR was registered based on these allegations.
The applicant is a 45-year-old doctor, not a flight risk, has deep roots in society, and has cooperated with investigation; an interim bail was granted on 03.09.2025.

The prosecution claims the applicant exploited the victim by promising marriage, obtained consent by fraud, is in possession of objectionable material, may circulate it, tamper with evidence, and influence witnesses.
The complainant (victim) is about 49 years old, has two daughters; the applicant has one son aged 18.
The court noted no violation of interim bail conditions, no threat to victim, and investigation is complete; mobile phone seized; custodial interrogation not necessary.
The court imposed conditions: not to enter Koregaon village, not tamper with evidence, not threaten the complainant, and any violation would permit cancellation of bail.

issues.text: Whether the anticipatory bail application should be granted in view of alleged offences under Sections 69 and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Whether consent obtained by fraud vitiates consent, making Section 69 applicable.
Whether the applicant poses a risk of tampering with evidence, influencing witnesses, or harassing the complainant, justifying denial of bail.

prosecution_arguments.text: The applicant exploited the victim by promising marriage, obtained consent by fraud, thus consent is vitiated and Section 69 BNS applies, punishable up to ten years.
The applicant possesses objectionable material and may circulate it to harass the victim.
The applicant may tamper with evidence and influence witnesses, posing a risk to the prosecution case.

defense_arguments.text: The applicant is falsely implicated; the FIR does not disclose any offence under Section 69 and the relationship was consensual.
The applicant is a 45-year-old doctor, not a flight risk, has deep societal roots, has complied with interim bail conditions, and is ready to abide by further conditions.
Investigation is complete, the mobile phone has been seized, and custodial interrogation is unnecessary.

judge_reasoning.text: The court examined the prosecution's case and found no violation of the interim bail conditions.
The applicant has cooperated with the investigation, has no flight risk, and has family responsibilities.
The risk of tampering with evidence or harassment can be mitigated by imposing strict conditions on bail.
Since the investigation is complete and custodial interrogation is unnecessary, there is no impediment to confirming the interim bail.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail is granted with conditions restricting movement, tampering with evidence, and threatening the complainant.

decision.summary: The court confirmed the interim bail order of 03.09.2025, imposed conditions restricting the applicant's movement, tampering with evidence, and threatening the complainant, and disposed of the application.

legal_principles.text: Consent obtained by fraud is not valid consent under criminal law.
Anticipatory bail may be granted if the applicant is not a flight risk and conditions can safeguard the investigation.
The court can impose conditions on bail to prevent tampering with evidence and intimidation of witnesses.
